title: Gene Fitness Landscapes and Cofitness Modules
scope: A gene fitness landscape is the set of growth effects that disrupting each gene produces across many experimental conditions.

title: Gene Essentiality and Perturbation-Assay Validity
scope: Gene essentiality is dependence of growth on a gene's function under a defined condition.

title: Laboratory Fitness Versus Natural Selection and Gene Conservation
scope: This topic asks whether a gene's measured effect on growth in the laboratory tells us why it is kept or lost across a species' genomes in nature.

title: Pangenome Structure and Genome Evolution
scope: A pangenome is the full set of gene clusters across the genomes of a species .

title: Ecotypes and Environmental Gene-Content Differentiation
scope: Within-species gene-content ecotypes are groups of genomes clustered by accessory (strain-variable) gene-content differences .

title: Metabolic Traits, Auxotrophy, and Community Dependence
scope: This topic asks what organisms can make, what they can use, and what they depend on others for.

title: Metabolic Models and Pathway-Level Evidence
scope: This topic asks how far genome-derived metabolic predictions can be trusted.

title: Lanthanide-Dependent Methylotrophy
scope: Lanthanide-dependent methylotrophy is the use of rare-earth elements (REEs, the lanthanides) as cofactors for methanol oxidation by pyrroloquinoline-quinone (PQQ) methanol dehydrogenases.

title: Functional Dark Matter and Annotation Resolution
scope: In this corpus, "dark" genes are genes that lack functional annotation: hypothetical proteins, DUFs (domains of unknown function) and uncharacterized proteins .

title: Resistance, Defense Systems, and Mobile Elements
scope: Bacteria carry overlapping systems for surviving chemical and biological attack: antimicrobial-resistance (AMR) genes, metal-tolerance determinants, anti-phage defense systems, and the mobile genetic elements (prophages, plasmids, integrative elements) that can move these functions between genomes.

title: Sampling Coverage and Statistical Confounding
scope: Many apparent ecological and genomic patterns in this corpus depend on who was sampled, what the reference databases could represent, and which observations were treated as independent.

title: Data Infrastructure, Provenance, and Research Practice
scope: This topic covers how data are organized, labelled and joined in the KBase Data Lakehouse, and how research practice (review, code history, ingestion) decides whether a result can be trusted.

title: Distributed Computation and Analysis Execution
scope: This topic covers how analyses actually run against the KBase Data Lakehouse: Spark (the distributed query engine behind the Lakehouse), the pandas frames and notebooks where results are examined, and the sessions, credentials and access paths between them.

title: Translational Microbiome and Phage Therapeutics
scope: This topic asks how microbiome measurements become interventions: which species to remove or displace, in which patients, with what evidence that the intervention will work and what it will cost the community.

title: Subsurface and Soil Community Ecology
scope: This topic asks what structures microbial communities in soils and the subsurface: depth and flow, contamination, treatment history, warming, and lineage-level genome content.
